input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only inspection right binding the Company (no other audit, verification or system-access provision exists; §1.4 runs in our favour). It already satisfies two fallback elements on its material terms — 30 days' prior written notice (exceeding the 15-day floor) and HDI bearing inspection costs unconditionally (better than a 10% underpayment shift) — and it is limited to normal business hours. However, it contains no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly, which fails the fallback and edges toward the walk-away position on unlimited audits. We therefore made the single minimal edit adding a once-per-twelve-month cap, leaving the favourable notice, business-hours and cost terms verbatim rather than upgrading to preferred wording.

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once in any twelve-month period
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a frequency cap so HDI's inspection right may be exercised no more than once in any twelve (12) month period; the existing 30 days' written notice, business-hours limit and HDI-borne costs already meet our position, so nothing else changes.
